structure:
A corpus of 103 Playwright trace zips of the GB notification service prototype's Design Release 2.1 (served under /design-release-2.1), recorded at Playwright 1.61.1 by the fit-style suite in workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/prototype-specs/e2e; all 103 tests passed, so no trace carries an error and the validation copy appears as rendered error states. index.json in the folder is the index: it maps each zip to its spec, test title, status and the pages (GET and POST) it visited. The traces come from 10 spec files: about-the-consignment (20 traces: notification type 3, origin of the import 4, what are you importing 5, germinal section 1 1, main import reason 7), address-book (9), consignment-parties (14: consignment addresses 7, add an address from the journey 2, add-address pages for the other roles 1, contact address 2, permanent address 2), dashboard (8), description-of-the-goods (7), documents (7), journeys (9: 4 notification-hub traces of 5 to 14 pages, and 5 end-to-end journeys of 48 to 58 pages and about 260 actions each), manage-notifications (7), templates (12, mostly 1 to 9 pages) and transport-and-arrival (10: add a transporter 4, arrival details 2, transit countries 1, transporter details 3); section traces run 1 to 43 pages and about 50 to 200 actions. The scope is every trace in the folder, so nothing is left out; the spec files themselves are a separate source (prototype:dr2-1-specs) and are named here only for their test titles. Cut into 16 parts along spec-file and describe seams in journey order: dashboard, the about-the-consignment describes in three parts, description of the goods, consignment parties in two, transport and arrival in two, documents, the hub, the five end-to-end journeys in two, manage notifications, templates, address book. The end-to-end journeys repeat pages the section parts also show; each part claims what its own traces render.

Extracted in 16 parts:
Part 1, Dashboards and drill-downs: Part 1, Dashboards and drill-downs: the 8 traces of dashboard.fit.spec.js, each opened and mined in full (Playwright 1.61.1, one page per navigation, 0 errors recorded). Traces and the pages they reach, in order: (1) overall dashboard › the prototype index lists every design release: /design-release-2.1/index, four release cards, the 'Start design release 2.1' link. (2) overall dashboard › /dashboard redirects: GET /design-release-2.1/dashboard 302 to /design-release-2.1, and /dashboard?tab=drafts 302 to /live-animals?tab=drafts. (3) overall dashboard › summarises every category: /design-release-2.1 (overall dashboard: intro, Messages, Create new, Use template, Live animals / Germinal products / Plants sections with glance cards and View dashboard links; the plants section is a placeholder linking to '#'). (4) category dashboards › live animals: /design-release-2.1/live-animals (Summary glance cards, Notifications search + sort, Additional filters panel with arrival-date radios, MOJ date pickers and status select, server-side tabs In progress / Draft / Completed with notification cards, and a search submitted as GET). (5) category dashboards › germinal products: /design-release-2.1/germinal-products (same layout, Number of packages instead of Number of animals; only the In progress tab opened). (6) at a glance drill-downs › action needed: /design-release-2.1/actions, unfiltered then ?category=live-animals. (7) drill-downs › inspection required: /design-release-2.1/inspection with its 'What to do at a border inspection' details opened. (8) drill-downs › status updated: /design-release-2.1/changes, unfiltered then ?category=germinal-products. Shared chrome claimed once: service navigation, phase banner, prototype footer. Every page is server-rendered by the prototype kit with no data API calls. Claims run page by page in that order (index, chrome, redirect, overall dashboard, live-animals dashboard, germinal dashboard, Action needed, Status updated, Inspection required, cross-page observations), then five later claims (119-123): the plants section's own style modifier, the index navigation with no current item, the date picker calendar, the card's accessible name, and category glance counts matching the drill-downs. Stops at links out of the dashboard: create-notification, templates, view/copy are other parts. Gaps recorded: sort effect, filter effect, pagination/empty states, germinal Draft/Completed tabs, unseen change types, the inspection drill-down's category view and entry point, Messages, and the plants dashboard.
Part 2, Notification type and origin of the import: Part 2, Notification type and origin of the import. Mined all 7 traces of about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js under the 'notification type' (3) and 'origin of the import' (4) describes, each opened in full with its action list, the expected values of its assertions (action detail), snapshots of the pages it rendered and, for the core and variant traces, the network log and form bodies. Traces (zip name under sources/traces-prototype, shortened here to the part after 'about-the-consignment--'): T1 notification-type-create-new-asks-what-is-being-imported-before-the-journey-starts (57 actions, validation + core); T2 notification-type-plants-for-planting-reaches-the-commodity-search-which-offers-nothing-to-pick (43, variant); T3 notification-type-starting-from-a-category-dashboard-skips-the-type-question (23, variant); T4 origin-of-the-import-country-is-optional-to-proceed-and-the-answers-are-kept (35, core); T5 origin-of-the-import-region-code-yes-reveals-the-code-box-with-the-country-prefix-and-an-empty-code-is-an-error (68, validation + variant); T6 origin-of-the-import-renders-the-origin-questions (44, core); T7 origin-of-the-import-the-country-search-offers-matching-countries-and-keeps-the-pick (37, variant). Page inventory in journey order: (1) /create-notification, a redirect only: with no category it 302s to /notification-type, with ?category=live-animals (the 'Create new' button on the live-animals dashboard) it 302s straight to /origin-of-the-import; (2) notification-type, 'What are you importing?' under the caption 'About the consignment', five radios and a Continue button, shown only when no category is given (T1 a16 and a30 error state, T2 a9); (3) origin-of-the-import, 'Origin of the import', always shown after the type: draft status and reference, country-of-origin search, region of origin code Yes/No with a conditional code box and country prefix, optional internal reference, Save and continue (T6 a28, T5 a32 error state, T7 a19 and a24, T4 a22 on return, T3 a10 from the dashboard); (4) what-are-you-importing, reached after origin, recorded here only as T2 renders it on the plants-for-planting branch (T2 a29): the rest of that page is part 3's. Conditional: the type question is skipped when the journey starts from a category dashboard; the region code box shows only when Yes is chosen; the code prefix fills only once a country is picked. The four types other than live animals and plants for planting are never chosen in any trace.
Part 3, What are you importing and germinal section 1: Part 3 mined all 6 traces from about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js in its 'what are you importing' (5) and 'germinal products: section 1' (1) describes: renders the commodity search for live animals (WAI-render, spec line 168), nothing selected is an error (WAI-error, 188), search lists the species of a commodity; ticking one adds it to the selection (WAI-search, 196), several commodities can be selected together, and cleared (WAI-several, 215), save and return to overview keeps the selection without validating (WAI-hub, 228), and category start, germinal search hint and the reduced list of reasons (GERM, 324). Trace refs below use the zip name's distinguishing tail. Every live-animals trace starts the same way: /design-release-2.1/create-notification redirects to notification-type, live-animals is checked, then origin-of-the-import is filled (France, no region code) and continued, landing on /design-release-2.1/what-are-you-importing. Pages, in journey order: (1) germinal category start: /design-release-2.1/create-notification?category=germinal-products redirects straight to origin-of-the-import, whose back link is /design-release-2.1/germinal-products (GERM only); (2) What are you importing? (all 6 traces): status bar (Draft tag and GBN-AG reference), caption 'About the consignment', h1, an ITAHC inset, a custom commodity search (label, hint, search input, search button, live results list of commodity headers with species checkboxes, a polite status region, a 'N selected' panel with per-commodity chips, Remove buttons and Clear all, four hidden inputs carrying the selection), a 'Help with commodity codes' details, Save and continue, Save and return to overview, Cancel and return to overview, back link to origin-of-the-import; its error state (WAI-error); the germinal variant of its hint and results (GERM); (3) Overview /design-release-2.1/notification-hub, reached by Save and return to overview with nothing selected (WAI-hub); (4) Main import reason, reached from a germinal selection (GERM), showing only Internal market (with its four purposes) and Transit. No commodity data request goes over the wire: commodity search runs in the page. Conditional: the germinal hint and results appear only on the germinal-products route; the selected panel and Clear all appear only once something is ticked; the error state only after Save and continue with no selection. Not walked anywhere in this part: removing a single chip, a search with no matches, ova or embryos searches, selecting a whole commodity rather than a species, and saving a real selection through Save and return to overview; each is a gap claim.
Part 4, Main reason for import: Part 4, Main import reason: the 7 traces of about-the-consignment.fit.spec.js › 'main import reason', every one opened and mined in full (actions, page requests, POST bodies, and DOM snapshots of each state). Traces: lists every reason with its hint (59 actions; reason page DOM at action 36, the pointer for the full page); a reason is optional to proceed (47 actions; POST at request 161, next page at action 34); internal market reveals the purposes and needs one (68 actions; reveal at 33, error at 45, success POST request 199); transhipment needs a destination country (67 actions; error at 44, POST 199); transit needs a port of exit and a destination country (67 actions; error at 43, POST 199); temporary admission horses needs a real exit date and a port of exit (76 actions; empty error at 44, 'real date' error at 57, both POST 200); the prototype seed route jumps straight to the reason page (46 actions; navigate at 31, redirect request 161, landing at 33). Every trace's beforeEach walks create-notification › live animals › origin (France, region code No) › commodity (cattle, Bos taurus) to /design-release-2.1/reason-for-import; those earlier pages belong to other parts. One page is in scope: reason-for-import ('Main import reason'), always shown for live animals after the commodity page. On it, one optional radios question (importReason, 5 reasons each with a hint) with four conditional reveals: Internal market › purpose radios (11 options, required once the reason is chosen); Transhipment or onward travel › destination country select (required); Transit › port of exit and destination country selects (both required); Temporary admission horses › exit date (MoJ date picker, required, must be a real date) and port of exit select (required). Re-entry has no reveal. Plus the seed route /design-release-2.1/prototype/reason-for-import. The slice stops at the page after the reason, consignment-details ('Commodity details'), which every successful submit reaches.
Part 5, Description of the goods: Part 5, Description of the goods: the 7 traces of description-of-the-goods.fit.spec.js, every one opened and its full action list read, with main-element HTML or text, back link, error summaries and inline errors snapshotted on every page in scope, and the network log read for the prototype's own requests. Trace aliases used in refs: ADD-CATTLE = additional-details-cattle-certification-purpose-and-unweaned-animals.zip (spec line 216, 71 actions); ADD-POULTRY = additional-details-poultry-no-identification-page-and-no-unweaned-question.zip (line 240, 59 actions); CD-CATTLE = commodity-details-cattle-number-of-animals-is-required-and-must-be-a-whole-number.zip (line 33, 97 actions); CD-GERMINAL = commodity-details-germinal-products-weight-packages-and-storage-temperature.zip (line 90, 83 actions); CD-TWO = commodity-details-two-commodities-get-one-block-each-removing-the-last-returns-to-the-search.zip (line 75, 66 actions); ID-CATTLE = identification-details-cattle-one-identification-panel-per-animal-saved-one-at-a-time.zip (line 120, 104 actions); ID-GERMINAL = identification-details-germinal-products-donor-dates-and-identification-mark-with-date-and-length-errors.zip (line 178, 80 actions). No trace recorded an error. Every trace walks notification type (live animals only), origin (France, no region), what are you importing and reason for import (Internal market, Breeding) to reach this section; those pages belong to other parts and are not claimed here. Pages in journey order: (1) Commodity details, /design-release-2.1/consignment-details, always shown, caption 'Description of the goods'; its fields differ by commodity: cattle, horse and pig get Number of animals plus Number of packages (when required), chicken gets Number of animals only, germinal products (cattle semen) get Total gross weight, Number of packages and a Temperature radio group; pointers CD-CATTLE action 40 (clean), 58 (blank error), 72 (zero error); CD-GERMINAL action 32 (clean), 45 (required errors), 58 (invalid errors); CD-TWO action 42 (two commodities), 52 (after removing horse), 53 (after removing pig, back on What are you importing?); ADD-POULTRY action 34 (chicken). (2) Identification details, /design-release-2.1/animal-identification-details, caption 'About the consignment', shown for cattle and germinal products, not for chicken; cattle get one Ear tag + Passport entry per animal saved one at a time, germinal products get one Donor name/ID, Collection date, Production date, Identification number/mark entry; pointers ID-CATTLE actions 44 (1 of 2), 60 (2 of 2), 72 (blank passport), 78 (all saved), 87 (after remove); ADD-CATTLE action 37 (1 of 1); ID-GERMINAL actions 38 (clean), 54 (errors). (3) Additional details, /design-release-2.1/additional-animal-details, caption 'Commodity details', shown for cattle and chicken, not for germinal products; cattle get certification purpose and unweaned animals, chicken get certification purpose only; pointers ADD-CATTLE action 46, ADD-POULTRY action 40. The section exits to Arrival details (/design-release-2.1/arrival-details), which belongs to another part. Integrations: the network log of every trace holds only the prototype's own server-rendered GET/POST page requests and the Prototype Kit's localhost:3011 socket traffic; no data API was called.
Part 6, Consignment addresses (the roles page and pickers): Part 6, consignment addresses: the 7 traces of consignment-parties.fit.spec.js › consignment addresses, every one opened and its full action list read. (1) cattle: five roles plus the CPH number (81 actions; roles page asserted at actions 37-62); (2) cat: permanent address replaces the CPH number (64 actions; roles page at 36-49, then a direct GET of /cph-number redirected to the roles page); (3) picking an address for every role, then the CPH number (208 actions, the core trace: each of the five pickers at actions 39-108, the place of origin country-search label at 109-111, choosing an address per role at 113-143, the CPH page at 145-162, a partial CPH at 164-171, a full CPH at 173-191, continue to the contact address at 193-195); (4) same as place of origin / same as consignee shortcuts (83 actions; roles page with shortcuts at 54, after applying them at 67); (5) the address search on a picker filters the list (61 actions; consignor picker filtered by 'Nordic' at 41-45); (6) a picker continued with nothing chosen returns to the roles page unchanged (55 actions; the importer picker at 38-42); (7) save and return to hub from a picker (55 actions; the consignee picker to the hub at 38-42). Every trace starts the same way (live animals, origin France, one species, Internal market / Breeding, a number of animals), then navigates straight to /design-release-2.1/roles-and-addresses; those earlier pages belong to other parts. Pages in this slice, in journey order: the Consignment addresses (roles) page /roles-and-addresses (always; six sections: Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination, then County parish holding (CPH) number for cattle or Permanent address for cats), five role pickers /place-of-origin, /consignor-or-exporter, /consignee, /importer and /place-of-destination (each reached from its 'Add a ...' or 'Change' link), and the CPH number page /cph-number (cattle only; redirected for a cat). Conditional surface: the CPH or permanent-address section by species; 'Same as place of origin' on the consignor and 'Same as consignee' on the importer and place of destination only when the source role is filled and the target empty; an inset address block and a 'Change' link once a role is filled; the place of origin picker's country search in place of the free-text search. The notification hub (reached by 'Save and return to hub') and the contact address page (reached by 'Save and continue' on a complete roles page) are other parts' pages and are claimed here only for the transitions. The add-address pages, the contact address and the permanent-address pages are part 7. Network logs read for every trace: only server-rendered document requests (GET 200, POST 302) and a local live-reload socket; no data call to any other system. Snapshots taken on the roles page (empty, with shortcuts, after shortcuts, complete, cat), on each picker, on the filtered consignor picker, on the CPH page and on the hub after a picker's save and return.
Part 7, Adding addresses, contact address and permanent address: Part 7 mined all 7 traces of four consignment-parties.fit.spec.js describes, each opened and its full action list read, with snapshots, evals and network logs taken on every page in scope. Trace names used in refs: [A] consignment-parties--add-an-address-from-the-journey-place-of-origin-an-international-address-entered-by-hand.zip (place of origin add-address, manual international entry, empty-submit errors, save and return to the picker); [B] consignment-parties--add-an-address-from-the-journey-consignee-a-uk-address-found-by-search-then-completed.zip (consignee add-address, UK lookup, empty-submit errors on the hidden fields, search 'Acorn', pick, complete contact details, save and select back to the roles page); [C] consignment-parties--add-address-pages-for-the-other-roles-consignor-is-entered-by-hand-importer-and-place-of-destination-search-uk-addresses.zip (consignor, importer and place of destination add-address pages opened from each picker's 'Add a new address' link, not submitted); [D] consignment-parties--contact-address-for-consignment-choose-the-contact-address.zip (contact address page, empty-submit error, choose an address, continue to review-notification); [E] consignment-parties--contact-address-for-consignment-add-a-new-branch-address-from-the-contact-page.zip (the 'add a new branch address' link to the address-book Add address details lookup page, not submitted); [F] consignment-parties--permanent-address-cat-one-choice-per-animal-same-as-destination-or-a-new-address.zip (2 cats; the per-animal Permanent address page, 'Add a place of destination before you can continue' error, new-address reveal and per-animal field errors, then a place of destination chosen and both animals set to same as POD, back to the roles page); [G] consignment-parties--permanent-address-the-enter-address-path-is-retired-and-lands-on-the-per-animal-page.zip (GET /permanent-address/enter-address redirects to /permanent-address/select). Each trace first walks the shared set-up (create notification, live animals, France, a commodity, Internal market / Breeding, a number of animals) to /roles-and-addresses; that set-up belongs to earlier parts and is not claimed here. Pages in this part, in journey position: (1) the add-address page 'Add address and contact details' at /<role>/add-address, reached from each role picker's 'Add a new address' link; it has two variants - manual international entry for place of origin and consignor (fields always shown, country select of 42 countries), and UK lookup for consignee, importer and place of destination (a 'Search for an address' box, address fields hidden until a result is picked, country fixed to United Kingdom); each variant shows a 'What else should this address be used for?' checkbox list of the role's sibling roles; (2) the place of origin picker as it renders after 'Save and return to address page' (success banner, new address in the list); (3) the roles page as it renders after 'Save and select' (success banner, the new address filled in for the role); (4) Contact address for consignment at /contact-address-for-consignment, radios of three addresses, error state, continue to /review-notification; (5) Add address details at /address-book/add/lookup (address book branch-address lookup, conditional on the contact page link); (6) Permanent address at /permanent-address/select, one card per animal (cat only), conditional reveal of a new-address form, two error states; (7) the roles page Permanent address row after saving. /permanent-address and /permanent-address/enter-address both redirect to /permanent-address/select. Address search made no network call. The role pickers themselves are part 6's and are claimed here only as the entry point. Surfaces the traces never reached are recorded as gaps.
Part 8, Arrival, transit countries and transporter selection: Part 8 of 16, Arrival, transit countries and transporter selection. Mined all 6 traces this part names, every action of each, from transport-and-arrival.fit.spec.js (read for test titles only): (1) arrival details › air and sea skip transit countries (64 actions, 0 errors); (2) arrival details › means of transport is the one required answer (105 actions, 0 errors, drives the error state); (3) transit countries › add and remove the countries the consignment travels through (103 actions); (4) transporter details › select a transporter from the list (85 actions); (5) transporter details › the legacy transport-details path redirects to the transporter page (65 actions); (6) transporter details › transporter is optional to proceed (66 actions). Every trace sets up the notification the same way (notification type live animals, origin France, chicken commodity, Internal market / Breeding, 100 animals) before navigating straight to /design-release-2.1/arrival-details; that set-up belongs to earlier parts and is not claimed here. Pages in journey order, all under /design-release-2.1/: (a) arrival-details, 'Arrival details', caption 'Transport and arrival', always shown; snapshot pointers: trace 1 action 44, trace 2 action 66 (error state), trace 6 action 46. (b) transit-countries, 'Which countries will the consignment travel through?', caption 'Movement', conditional: reached after Rail (trace 2 action 92) or Road (trace 3), and guarded with a redirect to the hub when means is Air (trace 1 action 50-51); pointers trace 3 actions 55, 70, 77, 88. (c) transporter, 'Transporter details', caption 'Transport and arrival', reached from arrival details after Air or from transit countries; pointers trace 4 action 60, trace 5 action 52. (d) the legacy /transport-details path, a 302 to /transporter (trace 5 request 319). Onward pages seen only as landing points: upload-documents ('Upload documents', trace 4 action 72, trace 6 action 53) and notification-hub ('Overview', trace 1 action 51). Integrations: the network logs show only same-origin prototype page GETs and form POSTs (bodies read for arrival-details, transit-countries, transporter); the port list (205 entries) is inlined in the arrival page HTML, the transit country list (41 entries) is inlined as application/json in the transit page, and the 8 transporters are server-rendered rows; no reference-data or API call fired. Adding a new transporter (/transporter/add) is part 9's and is claimed here only as the link that leads to it. Surfaces the traces never reached (Sea route, blank transit submit, date validation, transporter search, View details, Save and return, Cancel) are recorded as gaps.
Part 9, Add a transporter: Part 9, 'Add a transporter': the 4 traces of the transport-and-arrival.fit.spec.js 'add a transporter' describe, every one opened and mined (all passed, 0 errors). Refs use these short names: [type] = transport-and-arrival--add-a-transporter-choose-a-transporter-type.zip (spec line 168, 88 actions); [private] = transport-and-arrival--add-a-transporter-private-transporter-every-required-field-is-named-then-it-is-added-and-selectable.zip (line 184, 117 actions); [cancel] = transport-and-arrival--add-a-transporter-private-transporter-cancel-leaves-the-journey-for-the-dashboard.zip (line 219, 71 actions); [commercial] = transport-and-arrival--add-a-transporter-commercial-transporter-authorisation-number-address-search-or-manual-entry.zip (line 228, 116 actions). Every trace walks the same set-up (create notification, live animals, France, chicken, internal market / breeding, 100 animals, arrival details at Heathrow) and then: (1) Transporter details /design-release-2.1/transporter, the entry point, where 'Add a transporter' is clicked (action 50); (2) Choose a transporter type /transporter/add (always): two radios, Private transporter or Commercial; blank Continue gives an error; (3a) Add a private transporter /transporter/add/private (when Private): name, address lines, town, county, postcode, country select defaulting to United Kingdom, then 'Enter contact details' email and phone; blank save names 6 required fields; complete save returns to /transporter; (3b) Add a commercial transporter /transporter/add/commercial (when Commercial): an Important banner on authorisation, authorisation number, name, an address search with an 'Enter address manually' toggle revealing address lines and a country fixed to Northern Ireland, contact details revealed with the address; blank save names 7 required fields; complete save returns to /transporter; (4) Transporter details again, with a Success banner and the new transporter first in the list, already selected and tagged New; (5) Cancel and return to dashboard on the private page posts and lands on the Dashboard /design-release-2.1. Not reached by any trace: typing into the commercial address search, format validation of any field, cancel from the commercial page, and the back links being followed. Pointers: [type] actions 55 (page) and 68 (error); [private] actions 58-66 (page), 80 (error), 97 (list after add); [commercial] actions 59 (page), 72 (manual entry revealed), 83 (error), 102 (list after add), request 436 (POST body); [cancel] action 58 (dashboard). The spec file was read for test titles only.
Part 10, Upload documents: Part 10, Upload documents. Mined all 7 traces of documents.fit.spec.js (every action list read in full; snapshots, DOM evals and the network log of each): T1 renders-the-upload-guidance-and-document-fields (core render, 68 actions), T2 save-and-add-another-with-nothing-entered-names-every-field (validation), T3 a-date-of-issue-that-is-not-a-real-date (validation), T4 continuing-with-a-document-type-chosen-but-the-rest-blank-is-held-on-the-page (validation), T5 documents-are-optional-continuing-with-nothing-chosen-moves-on (variant), T6 upload-documents-from-the-hub-save-and-return-to-overview-from-the-hub (variant), T7 a-complete-document-is-listed-with-its-virus-check-status-and-can-be-removed (core journey). The spec file was read for test titles only. Every trace's before-hook starts a live-animals notification, answers origin (France, no region) and commodity (cattle), then navigates to /design-release-2.1/upload-documents; T6 instead answers origin only and enters from the Overview (notification hub) task list link. Pages in this slice: (1) Upload documents, /design-release-2.1/upload-documents, always: status strip (Draft tag plus GBN-AG reference), caption 'Documents', H1 'Upload documents', intro paragraph, bullet list of other documents, a 'Check which additional documents you must upload' details with a 3-row table and GOV.UK link, then a 'File upload' card section holding Document reference (text input), Document type (14-option select), Date of issue (MOJ date picker text input with hint), Attachment (custom drop zone over a file input with file requirements list), a 'Save and add another' button, the list of added documents (a table inside the card, shown only once a document is added) with a virus check status tag and a Remove button per row, then Save and continue, Save and return to overview and a Cancel and return to overview link. Error states on the same page: nothing entered (4 errors), not a real date, and type chosen but rest blank (3 errors). (2) Destinations: Save and continue with nothing chosen goes to Consignment addresses (/roles-and-addresses); entered from the hub (?from=hub), Save and continue returns to Overview (/notification-hub). Network: every submit is a same-route form POST (urlencoded, 302 then GET on success, 200 re-render on error); a client script posts to the unprefixed /upload-documents/virus-check/<id> after a document is added. Not reached: the Save and return to overview button, the Cancel link, the date picker dialog, any file type or size or file-count error, and any virus check outcome other than 'Scanning for virus'.
Part 11, The notification hub: Part 11, the notification hub: the four traces of journeys.fit.spec.js › the notification hub, each opened and mined in full (actions, network log, snapshots). (1) journeys--the-notification-hub-a-fresh-notification-lists-every-task-as-to-do (59 actions): create-notification 302 to notification-type, live-animals chosen, Continue lands on origin-of-the-import, then a direct navigate to /design-release-2.1/notification-hub; snapshot at action 37 is the fresh hub. (2) journeys--the-notification-hub-a-hub-task-link-returns-to-the-hub-after-saving (33 actions): fresh hub, click 'Main import reason' to /reason-for-import?from=hub (snapshot action 16), choose Re-entry, Save and continue, back on the hub with that task 'Complete' (snapshot action 20). (3) journeys--the-notification-hub-review-with-tasks-missing-lists-each-incomplete-section (63 actions): origin (France, no region), what-are-you-importing (cattle, Bos Taurus), reason (Internal market, Breeding), consignment-details (1 animal), then a direct navigate to /review-notification (snapshot action 37 to 47) and Continue, which re-renders the review (snapshot action 50). (4) journeys--the-notification-hub-the-submitted-page-is-guarded-until-the-declaration-is-confirmed (27 actions): a fresh notification, direct navigate to /notification-submitted, 302 to /declaration (snapshot action 14). claims.statement: The hub, task pages and review are served by a GOV.UK Prototype Kit app with no data calls to other services: every answer is a form post to the prototype, and state is held in the prototype's session.
claims.quote: x-powered-by: Express; Cookie: govuk-prototype-kit-[REDACTED]
claims.note: Inferred from the network logs of all four traces showing only page loads, form posts, static assets and the kit's browser-sync socket. The session cookie value is redacted.

claims.statement: No trace in this slice shows a task in any state other than 'To do' or 'Complete', such as 'In progress' after a partial answer.
claims.ref: journeys.fit.spec.js › the notification hub (all four traces)

claims.statement: No trace in this slice presses 'Save and return to overview', so where it goes and whether it saves a partial answer are not shown.
No trace in this slice clicks 'Review and submit' or 'Return to dashboard' on the hub; only their link targets are seen.
No trace in this slice shows the commodities cards with non-zero totals, so how animal and package totals are counted is not shown.
No trace in this slice follows the review's Delete button, so the delete confirmation and its outcome are not shown.
No trace in this slice submits the declaration with the box unticked, so its validation error copy is not shown here.
No trace in this slice reaches the notification-submitted page itself, so its content once the declaration is confirmed is not shown here.
The hub is shown only for a live-animals notification in this slice; whether other notification types get the same sections and tasks is not shown.
claims.ref: journeys.fit.spec.js › the notification hub (all four traces start with notificationType live-animals)

claims.quote: Animals for reproduction. This includes animals intended to contribute to the genetic pool of a breeding program, improve livestock quality, or produce offspring.

claims.statement: The hint for 'Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift' explains it covers any sale or transfer of ownership, including gifts.

claims.quote: Any movement of an animal that has as its aim the sale of or the transfer of ownership of the animal from one person or entity to another. For example, animals that have been sold and are being moved to a new owner or will be sold once in Great Britain, purchases from a breeder/shop overseas and where an animal is being moved to a new owner with no sale involved (for example a gift).

claims.note: Inferred from the network logs of all nine traces: only page GETs and form POSTs to the prototype on localhost:3010, plus the kit's dev socket. Each trace starts with a fresh seed (23 origin entries), so the state is per session. The rebuild needs a real address book store.

claims.statement: The add-address, entry and delete pages use GOV.UK components (caption, heading, inputs, select, checkboxes, summary list, buttons, button group, error summary, notification banner) with custom wrapper classes; the choose-type page reuses a class from the reason-for-import radios.

claims.note: The custom pieces are layout wrappers, the type-ahead address search, and custom heading classes on the list, choose-type and edit pages.

claims.note: In every trace the uses are asked on the add-address page itself.

claims.statement: No trace completes saving a Destination, Consignee or Importer or a Branch address, so the save, the uses validation and the banner for those types are not shown.
No trace opens the 'Enter address manually' route on the UK search layout, or searches with no matching address.
No trace changes the Type filter, searches with no match on the list, or visits page 3, so filtering by type, an empty-results message and the last page are not shown.
No trace opens, edits or deletes a Transporter, Destination or Branch entry, so their entry pages (and whether a transporter shows its approval number and type) are not shown.
No trace drives format validation of email address, phone number or postcode, or a length limit on any field; only blank-field messages are shown.
No trace uses the edit page's 'Cancel' button, the delete page's 'No, cancel' link or the add page's 'Cancel and return to address book' link, so where they land is only known from their hrefs.
